messages:
alex: quick heads-up — canary flip 176801... metrics look off. SRM test p=0.003, variant B traffic is 43% vs expected 50% :thinking:
deploy-bot: canary started at 1768012345, 20% traffic -> variant A, 20% -> variant B
analytics-bot: snapshot: A_users=9,812, B_users=7,660, conversions A=982, B=774, calc SRM p=0.003
miriam: @alex that's a big SRM. first thing: did we change the bucketing key or SDK recently?
rui: run sample ratio test SQL: ```select variant, count(*) from events where exp='canary_042' group by variant;``` check by region and client_version
sam: also check sticky cookie TTL. if cookies expired earlier some users might re-bucket causing undercount
irene: quick check — I see a rollout policy routing by region for APAC fallback to cheaper pool. that could skew numbers if APAC users biased towards B
alex: good call @irene. I didn't realize region fallback applied to this canary. I pushed a policy tweak yesterday for latency guarding
miriam: ok we need to decide end criteria. options: 1) pause and fix instrumentation, 2) continue and apply sequential correction. I prefer pause until SRM < 0.01 or we verify no infra bias
rui: for stopping rules: require min N per arm (we usually use 20k), p<0.05 with correction (we use alpha spending / Pocock) OR posterior prob > 0.975 for Bayesian
sam: for short term let's: pause ramp to 50%, run diagnostics (bucket hash, cookie, region distribution), re-run with stratified sampling by region
analytics-bot: diagnostic query suggestions: ```-- SRM by region select region, variant, count(*) from events where exp='canary_042' group by region, variant;``` and ```-- check client builds select client_version, variant, count(*) ...``` 
alex: action items: (1) disable region fallback from policy for this canary — @irene can you revert? (2) @rui run SRM-by-region query and post results (3) @miriam hold ramp and update docs
irene: reverting fallback now :white_check_mark:
rui: posted SRM-by-region: NA p=0.4, EU p=0.6, APAC p=0.0008 — APAC is where variant B undersampled, looks like routing misapply
miriam: thanks. that suggests routing bug. I'm pausing the rollout and tagging incident. we should block further canaries until we add a pre-rollout SRM check in the console
sam: +1 on console guard: check expected split per region, min samples, and warn if SRM p<0.01. add link to run diagnostics before ramp
alex: final call: pause canary, rollback policy tweak, re-run with stratified ramp and SRM check. let's aim for automated guard in 2 sprints
miriam: logging the decision and tasks in the rollout repo /projects/rollouts/issues/124 :memo:
alex: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
